description: pkix-lint/src/cabf_tls_br.rs:586: CabfTlsBrProfile::lint_runner() calls all_lints() on every invocation, allocating Vec<Box<dyn Lint>> fresh each time. Meanwhile, lints() returns a &[Box<dyn Lint>] from a static OnceLock (cheap). The asymmetry is documented but not obvious to callers. A caller in a hot path (e.g., per-TLS-handshake) who calls profile.lint_runner() will burn heap allocations on every connection. The doc says 'cache the returned LintRunner' but this is a maintainer trap — the caller has to know to do this. The fix is to either return &LintRunner from a static OnceLock, or clearly mark lint_runner() with #[must_use = 'cache this runner'].
notes: lint_runner() doc at lib.rs:783 explicitly tells implementors to document caching behavior and tells callers to cache themselves. This is correct API design — the trait cannot enforce it.
title: LintProfile::lint_runner() allocates fresh on every call despite lints() being cached
